Name: Barlov's Portraiture
Author: BarlovMonkiss
Description:
[b][size=5]Barlov's Portraiture[/size][/b]
[list=1]
[*]Developed from scratch[i], this is a full replacement for [b]Portraiture + PortraiturePlus[/b], [/i]and is built around content packs.[/*]
[*]It replaces the dialogue portrait system with six configurable display modes, a content-pack framework for [b]portraits/scenes/borders/namebars/weather[/b], and a redesigned shop-portrait renderer.[/*]
[*]It ships with some basic bundled defaults (backgrounds/weather/frame/namebar), but content packs would flesh it out more.[/*]
[*][b]Room-Level Location[/b][b] Support [/b][b]:[/b] Yes, it exists, but it's limited because I have to add rooms to the code manually.[/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]Main Features[/heading]
[size=4][u]Display Modes[/u][/size]
Cycle through six ways dialogue portraits can render on screen:
[list]
[*][b]InFrame[/b] — classic in-box portrait[/*]
[*][b]Expanded[/b] — larger configurable portrait box[/*]
[*][b]Clean In Place[/b] — same as Expanded, but without the frame and background[/*]
[*][b]Clean Left[/b] — no frame, floats above the box, anchored to the left[/*]
[*][b]Clean[/b] — no frame, floats above the box, centered[/*]
[*][b]Clean Right[/b] — no frame, floats above the box, anchored to the right[/*]
[/list][size=4][u]Content Packs[/u][/size]
[list]
[*]Everything visual — portraits, scenes, borders, namebars, and weather overlays — is driven by content packs using a shared [color=#e06666]content.json[/color] format, with location/season/time/weather-aware resolution so packs can target specific contexts (e.g. a Forest-only rainy-day scene) without extra code. A bundled generator script is included for pack authors — see[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Weather Layer: Animated weather overlays render behind portraits, with crossfade transitions when necessary and automatic fallback to vanilla weather art when a pack doesn't cover the current condition.[/*]
[/list][list]
[*]Redesigned Shop Portraits:  Clean, no frame, expanded portraits. Includes support for the PIF Magician's shop. He deserved a portrait.[/*]
[/list][b]Keybinds [/b](GMCM rebindable)
[list]
[*][font=Courier New]Cycle display mode: [color=#e06666]I[/color][/font][/*]
[*][font=Courier New]Cycle portrait pack: [color=#e06666]P[/color][/font][/*]
[*][font=Courier New]Cycle scene pack: [color=#e06666]Ctrl + P[/color][/font][/*]
[*][font=Courier New]Cycle border pack: [color=#e06666]Alt + P[/color][/font][/*]
[*][font=Courier New]Cycle namebar pack: [color=#e06666]Shift + P[/color][/font][/*]
[*][font=Courier New]Cycle weather pack: [color=#e06666]Ctrl + Alt + P[/color][/font][/*]
[*][font=Courier New]Freeze current NPC's pack: [color=#e06666]O[/color][/font][/*]
[*][font=Courier New]Freeze current weather pack: [/font][color=#e06666][font=Courier New]Ctrl + Alt + O[/font][/color][/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]Requirements[/heading]
[list]
[*][b]SMAPI[/b] 4.0 or later[/*]
[*][b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] — required dependency[/*]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]Installation[/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI [/url]if you haven't already.[/*]
[*]Uninstall Portraiture and/or PortraiturePlus[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/24534] [/url]if present.[/*]
[*]Download this mod and unzip it into your [color=#e06666]Stardew Valley/Mods[/color] folder, or to a nested folder within it.[/*]
[*]Install Generic Mod Config Menu.[/*]
[*]Launch the game.[/*]
[/list][line]
[heading]For Content Pack Authors[/heading]
Barlov's Portraiture reads content packs from [color=#e06666]Mods/[/color] the same way any SMAPI content pack works. Packs can supply portraits, scenes, borders, namebars, and/or weather art independently — you don't need to provide all five.

[i]Note: I've added Room support to the location tags for things that support location.
[/i]
[list]
[*][i]That means [color=#e06666]HaleyHouse_EmilyBedroom.png[/color] > [color=#e06666]HaleyHouse.png[/color].[/i][/*]

[b][u][size=4]Adding Room support to your mod[/size][/u][/b]
[spoiler]Rooms have to be hard coded, but you can easily add support for to your mod.
[b][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1915]Content Patcher[/url] is required[/b][b] to make this work[/b]!

[b][u][size=4]New Buildings/Locations[/size]
[/u][/b][size=3]You will need a folder in your mod with a dedicated [color=#e06666]manifest.json[/color] and a [color=#e06666]content.json[/color] .
The manifest declares that you are creating a content pack.[/size]

[size=4][b][u][color=#6aa84f]manifest.json[/color][/u][/b][/size]

[code]{
  "Name": "New Rooms For Barlov's Portraiture",
  "Author": "YourNameHere",
  "Version": "1.0.0",
  "Description": "Example Content Patcher pack.",
  "UniqueID": "YourName.ExampleBarlovsPortraitureRooms",
  "MinimumApiVersion": "4.0.0",
  "ContentPackFor": {
    "UniqueID": "Pathoschild.ContentPatcher"
  },
  "UpdateKeys": []
}[/code]Here is an example content.json intending to add support for 2 new buildings.
[list]
[*]It would add a Town Bank and Sheriff's Office room mapping.[/*]
[*]You will notice the the "SheriffOffice_Office" is irregularly shaped and requires two entries to cover it.[/*]
[/list][b][u][color=#6aa84f][size=4]content.json[/size][/color][/u][/b]
[code]{
  "Format": "2.0.0",
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "EditData",
      "Target": "Mods/BarlovsPortraiture/Rooms",
      "Entries": {
        "TownBank": [
          { "Left": 0,  "Top": 0,  "Right": 20, "Bottom": 8,  "Room": "Lobby" },
          { "Left": 0,  "Top": 9,  "Right": 8,  "Bottom": 16, "Room": "Vault" },
          { "Left": 9,  "Top": 9,  "Right": 20, "Bottom": 16, "Room": "ManagerOffice" }
        ],

        "SheriffOffice": [
          { "Left": 0,  "Top": 0,  "Right": 14, "Bottom": 6,  "Room": "Office" },
          { "Left": 0,  "Top": 7,  "Right": 6,  "Bottom": 14, "Room": "Office" },
          { "Left": 15, "Top": 0,  "Right": 20, "Bottom": 6,  "Room": "Armory" },
          { "Left": 7,  "Top": 7,  "Right": 20, "Bottom": 14, "Room": "JailCells" }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}[/code][b][u][size=4]Updating existing location maps[/size][/u][/b]
[i](to order to add or adjust rooms)[/i]
It is exactly the same method as adding a completely new location, with exceptions.
[list=1]
[*]You must specify the ingame name of the location, the same as adding a new location.[/*]
[*]Adding the entry will OVERWRITE the previous entry for that location.[/*]
[*]That means if you add a new room (like a bathroom), you must also [b]include all of the old rooms as well[/b], or they will disappear from the room table.[/*]
[*][i]This also means that two mods changing the map data for a single location will conflict, with the second to fire overwriting the first.[/i][/*]
[/list][b][u][size=4]Double Content Packs[/size][/u][/b]
If your mod will be a content pack for BOTH location sub-mapping and portraits/scenes/frames/etc, you'll need do something like this:

MyCoolNewMod/
├──  MyCoolNewModStuff/
│  ├── manifest.json        
│  └── content.json        
├── BarlovsPortraiture.ArtPack/
│  ├── manifest.json        <- ContentPackFor: "Barlov.Portraiture"
│  ├── content.json        <- this mod's own portrait/scene/border schema
│  └── assets/
└── BarlovsPortraiture.RoomsPatch/
    ├── manifest.json        <- ContentPackFor: "Pathoschild.ContentPatcher"
    └── content.json        <- CP's "Changes"/"EditData" schema, editing Mods/BarlovsPortraiture/Rooms[/spoiler]


[size=4][u][b]Portraits[/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler]
[size=5][b]1. Folder structure[/b][/size]
[code]YourPackName/
├── manifest.json          <- SMAPI's manifest — ContentPackFor: "Barlov.Portraiture"
├── content.json            <- generated for you, see step 3
└── assets/
    └── portraits/
        ├── Abigail/
        │   ├── Abigail.png
        │   ├── Abigail_Rain.png
        │   └── Abigail_spring.png
        ├── Haley/
        │   └── Haley.png
        └── ...[/code][font=Arial]Each NPC gets their own subfolder under [  assets/portraits/  ], named exactly after their internal game name (e.g. Abigail, Haley, Lewis).[/font]
[font=Arial]Every file inside that subfolder [b]repeats the character's name as a prefix[/b], even though it's already inside their folder — this isn't redundant, it's how the resolver identifies the file.

[color=#e06666]Abigail/Rain.png[/color]  will not work, but this will:  [color=#e06666]Abigail/Abigail_Rain.png[/color] .[/font]

[heading][size=5]2. Filename rules[/size][/heading]
Here's the priority chain from highest to lowest:
[list=1]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_event{ID}.png [/color]— a specific event/cutscene[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_Wedding.png [/color]— player's wedding[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Festival}_{Year}.png[/color] — a specific festival, specific year[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Festival}.png[/color] — that festival, any year[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Location}_{Season}_{Year}_{Day}.png[/color] — exact location + date[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Location}_{Season}_{Day}.png[/color] — location + season + day[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Location}_{Season}.png[/color] — location + season[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Location}_{Day}.png[/color] — location + day[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Location}.png[/color] — any time in that location[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Season}_Rain.png[/color] — raining, that season[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Season}_Indoor.png /_Outdoor.png[/color] — indoors/outdoors, that season[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Season}_{Year}_{Day}.png[/color] — season + exact date[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Season}_{Day}.png[/color] — season + day[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Season}.png[/color] — that season, any time[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_Rain.png[/color] — raining, any season[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}.png[/color] — base fallback[/*]
[/list][b]Note[/b]: hour-range files ( [color=#e06666]{Character}_HHMM-HHMM.png[/color] and its location/season-scoped variants) are interleaved into this chain at each corresponding level — the code checks the hour-range version right before the plain version at that specificity tier.

If the mod can't find anything, it reverts to vanilla portrait.
To avoid that, either include [color=#e06666]{Character}.png[/color] as the default portrait or [color=#e06666]{Character}_{Season}.png[/color] for each season.

Everything past that is optional layers of specificity. Add underscores to narrow when a portrait should show. The resolver tries the most specific match first and falls back down the list until something exists:

You only need to provide the specificity levels you actually care about — a pack with just [color=#e06666]Abigail.png[/color] and [color=#e06666]Abigail_Rain.png[/color] is completely valid.
Anything not covered falls through to the next-broadest file you [i]did[/i] provide.

[size=4][b]Location[/b] and [b]Festival[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Names are the game's internal names, not display names.[/*]
[*]Town, Farm, Beach, not "Pelican Town."[/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Season[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter.[/*]
[/list][b][size=4]Shop portrait override[/size][/b]
[list]
[*]If you want a different portrait specifically for when this NPC is running a shop, add [color=#e06666]{Character}_shop.png[/color].[/*]
[*]It's checked before everything else in the table above, but only in shop contexts — it won't affect normal dialogue.[/*]
[/list][b][size=4]Time-of-day ranges[/size]
[/b] Hours use 24-hour military time.
For portraits that should only appear during specific hours, use:
[list]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_HHMM-HHMM.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Location}_HHMM-HHMM.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Character}_{Season}_HHMM-HHMM.png[/color][/*]
[/list]e.g.
[list]
[*][color=#e06666]Abigail_Winter_1800-2400.png[/color][/*]
[/list]Which shows from 6 PM up to (not including) midnight during the winter.
If two hour-range files both match the current time, the [b]narrower[/b] range wins
[list]
[*]So a 1200-1300 file beats a 0600-1800 file that also covers that hour.[/*]
[/list][size=5][b]3. Generating content.json [/b][/size]
Don't hand-write content.json, run the bundled generator instead. 
[list=1]
[*]Copy [color=#e06666]run_to_generate_content_json.py[/color] ([i]from misc downloads[/i]) into your pack's root folder (next to manifest.json).[/*]
[*]Open it and set [color=#e06666]MOD_UNIQUE_ID[/color] to your [b]own[/b] pack's unique ID ([i]from your manifest.json[/i]), not Barlov.Portraiture .[/*]
[*]Run it. It scans your assets/ folder and writes a matching content.json automatically — you don't need to list files by hand.[/*]
[*]Re-run it any time you add or rename files.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]

[b][u][size=4]Scenes[/size][/u][/b]
[spoiler][heading][size=5]1. Folder structure[/size][/heading]
[code]YourPackName/
├── manifest.json
├── content.json
└── assets/
    └── scenes/
        ├── Beach_Sunset.png
        ├── Town.png
        ├── Town_Winter_Night_Cloudy.png
        ├── Forest.png
        ├── Forest_Kana.WeatherWonders_AcidRain.png
        ├── Winter.png
        └── Background.png[/code][list]
[*]Scenes live under  "assets/scenes". Unlike portraits, splitting scenes into subfolders is optional and you can name them whatever you want.[/*]
[*]The resolver scans recursively and matches on filename alone, so [color=#e06666]Forest/Forest.png[/color] works exactly the same as a top-level [color=#e06666]Forest.png[/color].[/*]
[*]Just don't put the same bare filename in two different subfolders — if you do, whichever one the system happens to scan last silently wins, with no warning.[/*]
[/list][heading][size=5]2. Filename rules [/size]
[size=3]Everything is case-insensitive. 
The resolver tries the most specific combination first and falls back from there. For a given location, in order:[/size][/heading]
[list=1]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}_{TimeOfDay}_{Weather}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}_{TimeOfDay}.png [/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}_{Weather}.png [/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}.png [/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{TimeOfDay}_{Weather}.png [/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{TimeOfDay}.png [/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Weather}.png [/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}.png [/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Season}_{Weather}.png [/color](if outdoors)[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Season}.png [/color](if outdoors)[/*]
[*][color=#e06666]B[/color][color=#e06666]ackground.png[/color][/*]
[/list]If those fail, it defaults to this mod's generic bundled scenes.

[spoiler][size=5][b]1. Folder structure[/b][/size]
[code]YourPackName/
├── manifest.json
├── content.json
└── assets/
    └── borders/
        ├── Town.png
        ├── Town_winter.png
        ├── winter.png
        └── border.png[/code]Files live directly under [color=#e06666]assets/borders/[/color]; subfolders are optional. Matching is recursive and by bare filename only, so avoid duplicate filenames across subfolders (last one found silently wins).
[heading][size=5]2. Filename rules[/size]
[size=3]Everything is case insensitive. [/size][/heading]
Same chain as scenes, minus the location-category tier — there's no Forest/Farm grouping for borders. In order, most to least specific:
[list=1]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}_{TimeOfDay}_{Weather}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}_{TimeOfDay}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}_{Weather}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Season}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{TimeOfDay}_{Weather}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{TimeOfDay}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}_{Weather}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Location}.png[/color][/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Season}_{Weather}.png [/color](outdoor only) [/*]
[*][color=#e06666]{Season}.png [/color](outdoor only) [/*]
[*][color=#e06666]Border.png[/color][/*]
[/list][b][size=4]TimeOfDay[/size]
[/b]
[list=1]
[*][color=#e06666]Sunset, Night[/color][/*]
[*]{blank, default state}[/*]
[/list][b][size=4]Weather[/size][/b]
[list=1]
[*][color=#e06666]Rain, Storm, Snow, Wind, GreenRain,[/color] or a modded weather ID if a weather mod is installed. Example: [color=#e06666]Kana.WeatherWonders_AcidRain[/color] . [/*]
[*][color=#e06666]Cloudy [/color](generic fallback for overcast days)[/*]
[*]{blank, which is default}[/*]
[/list][b][size=4]Indoor locations[/size][/b]
[list]
[*]Indoor locations skip both season and weather entirely, falling straight to [color=#e06666]location.png [/color]and [color=#e06666]border.png[/color][/*]
[/list][b][size=5]3. Generating content.json [/size][/b]
Don't hand-write content.json, run the bundled generator instead. 
[list=1]
[*]Copy run_to_generate_content_json.py ([i]from misc downloads[/i]) into your pack's root folder (next to manifest.json).[/*]
[*]Open it and set MOD_UNIQUE_ID to your [b]own[/b] pack's unique ID ([i]from your manifest.json[/i]), not Barlov.Portraiture .[/*]
[*]Run it. It scans your assets/ folder and writes a matching content.json automatically — you don't need to list files by hand.[/*]
[*]Re-run it any time you add or rename files.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]
[b][u][size=4]Portrait Weather Animations[/size][/u][/b]
[spoiler][heading][size=5]1. Folder structure[/size][/heading]
[code]YourPackName/
├── manifest.json
├── content.json
└── assets/
    └── weather/
        ├── Rain.png
        ├── Rain.json
        ├── Snow.png
        └── Snow.json[/code]Each weather type is a [b]matched pair[/b]: a [color=#e06666].png sprite sheet[/color] and a [color=#e06666].json sidecar[/color] with frame timing. 


[heading][size=5]2. Filenames = exact weather IDs[/size][/heading]

[/list]— e.g.

[/list][b]Generic in-code Fallbacks: [/b]
[list]
[*][color=#e06666]Rain[/color]: ( Storm, GreenRain, Kana.WeatherWonders_Deluge, Kana.WeatherWonders_Drizzle, Kana.WeatherWonders_Hailstorm, Kana.WeatherWonders_MuddyRain,  Kana.WeatherWonders_AcidRain, Kana.WeatherWonders_RainSnowMix )[/*]

[/list][b][size=5]3. Animation Sheet Creation[/size][/b]
[heading][size=4]Step 1: Draw a transparent, square GIF[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*]Make your animation in your preferred image editor as a transparent-background, [b]square [/b].gif. [b]Don't build the sprite sheet by hand[/b].[/*]
[/list][heading][size=4]Step 2: Convert it using  gif_to_spritesheet.py[/size][/heading]
[list=1]
[*]Install PythonGo: easy to miss but required for the next steps to work. to python.org/downloads and get the latest Python 3 installer. Run it, and make sure to check the box that says "Add python.exe to PATH" before clicking Install — this step is easy to miss but required for the next steps to work.[/*]
[*]Install Pillow: Open Command Prompt (search "cmd" in the Start menu) and type: pip install pillow — then press Enter. This installs the one extra library the script needs to read and write image files.[/*]
[*]Run the script on your GIF: Put gif_to_spritesheet.py in the same folder as your .gif file. In Command Prompt, cd to that folder, then run: python gif_to_spritesheet.py YourAnimation.gif — this writes YourAnimation.png and YourAnimation.json right next to it.[/*]
[*]Place both files (png & json) in your mod assets folder or subfolder.[/*]
[/list][heading][size=4]Optional: loop crossfade [/size][/heading]
If your animation doesn't loop cleanly (a visible jump from last frame back to first), open the generated [color=#e06666]json[/color] and add:
[code]"CrossfadeMs": -1[/code]CrossfadeMs

[*][color=#e06666]0[/color] (or omit it) : No crossfade — the default. [/*]
[/list]Example:
[code]{

[b][size=4][u]Namebar Pack[/u][/size][/b]
[spoiler][b][size=5]1. Folder structure[/size][/b]
[code]YourPackName/
├── manifest.json
├── content.json
└── assets/
    └── namebars/
        ├── Autumn.png
        ├── Winter.png
        └── Board.png[/code][heading][size=5]2. How it works[/size][/heading]
[list]
[*]Every [color=#e06666].png[/color] you put in [color=#e06666]assets/namebars/[/color] becomes one entry in the player's cycle list (default keybind Shift+P).[/*]
[*]Namebars are universal; there's no matching logic at all — no location, season, weather, or NPC context.[/*]
[*]Each file is just one alternative full-bar image, shown by name in the cycle (e.g. "Your Pack — Autumn").[/*]
[/list]Standard size is [b]1024×181px[/b] so a namebar drops in as a like-for-like swap of the bundled default, but any size works — the renderer measures and stretches each image itself.
[heading][size=4]Optional: cap width override [/size][/heading]
The renderer auto-detects each end's "cap" (the non-stretching decorative edge) by scanning the image's alpha channel for where it stabilizes. That works well for art with a distinct end-cap shape, but can misjudge art where the cap is a fully opaque rectangle whose edge is only implied by painted shading (e.g. a wood-grain board) — the auto-detected cap can come out too narrow, crowding the name text against the edge.

If that happens with your art, add a same-named [color=#e06666].json [/color]sidecar next to the image:
[code]{
  "CapWidth": 120
}[/code]CapWidth is in the same raw pixel units as your source image. This is optional — skip it entirely unless your namebar actually looks crowded at the edges in-game.

[*]Run it. It scans your assets/ folder and writes a matching content.json automatically — you don't need to list files by hand.[/*]
[*]Re-run it any time you add or rename files.[/*]
[/list][/spoiler]
